title: Hold the Line
intro: What decides a long set is how long you can stay at the edge of hard. This trains that edge, and it does it on a bike, so nothing lands. If your legs have already taken a lot of court this week, this is a hard session that adds fitness without adding more stops.

Five efforts of four minutes. Hard but controlled, the kind where you can get a short sentence out but not a long one. If you're down to single words, ease off a little but keep it hard. If you could chat freely, add a bit of resistance on the next one. Between each one, spin easy for two minutes and keep pedalling. Cutting the rest short turns it into a different session. Keep your legs turning quickly rather than grinding a heavy gear. A rower does the same job, and so does a treadmill on a steep incline. No machine? Walk up a steep hill for the four minutes and stroll back down for the two. First time through, stop after three efforts. Keep it 48 hours clear of a match. Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right means stop now and get it looked at before you train again. If a doctor has told you to be careful with hard exercise, check with them before you do this one.

before.text: Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right. Get it looked at before you train again. Told to be careful with hard exercise? Check with your doctor first.

good: Set the seat so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of each stroke
Keep it easy enough to breathe through your nose
bad: A seat set so low that your knees pinch up at the top of the stroke

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor with Overhead Reach

good: Squeeze the back glute, then reach the same-side arm overhead
Feel it at the front of the back hip
bad: Arching your lower back to feel more

good: Drive the knee forward over your toes
Feel the stretch low in the calf and the front of the ankle
bad: Letting the heel lift or the arch collapse

good: Push the floor away through your heels
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top
bad: Arching your lower back to lift higher

good: Add a little resistance on each one and keep the same cadence
Feel your legs load up without any strain
bad: Going hard on the first one

exercises.name: Threshold Effort
exercises.note: If you can't hold the same cadence at the same resistance for a whole effort, that was your last one.

good: Hold one steady cadence and one resistance for all four minutes
Your breathing should be hard but steady, never gasping
bad: Grinding a heavy gear at a slow cadence

good: Ease the resistance right off and keep the legs turning
Your heart rate should settle a little every minute
bad: Stopping pedalling the moment the last effort ends
